title: Digging Up the Past: Big Question Opener
bigQuestion: How can we explore the past?

nikos.name: Nikos
nikos.persona: cheerful 11-year-old boy, curious and full of questions

anna.name: Anna
anna.persona: clever 12-year-old girl, loves history and asks thoughtful questions

focusWords.kidDefinition: A report on TV or radio about recent events.
examples: My parents always watch the evening news report.
Today's news report says a new old city was found.
focusWords.greekHint: Δελτίο ειδήσεων: σκέψου το δελτίο των οκτώ.

focusWords.kidDefinition: An old object made by people, such as a pot or a tool.
examples: The archaeologists discovered many artifacts in the ancient tomb.
This clay artifact is three thousand years old.

focusWords.kidDefinition: A figure of a person or animal, carved or made from stone or metal.
examples: My favourite statue is Niki of Samothraki.
An archaeologist found a huge statue of a lion on the island.
focusWords.greekHint: Statue: άγαλμα, σαν τον Νίκη της Σαμοθράκης.

focusWords.kidDefinition: A hard, solid piece of the earth, like a rock.
examples: Zoe wore a necklace with precious stones.
Ancient builders cut huge stones to make the temple walls.

focusWords.kidDefinition: A unit for measuring length. One metre is about one big step.
examples: An archaeologist on Naxos island found a statue eleven metres tall!
The wall is two metres high.

focusWords.kidDefinition: A decorated covering worn on the head, often for a special occasion.
examples: If you visit the museum, you can see the headdresses women wore in old times.
The king wore a gold headdress at the festival.
focusWords.greekHint: Headdress: κορδέλα ή μαντήλι για το κεφάλι.

focusWords.kidDefinition: The changing of words from one language into another language.
examples: Is this translation of the article correct?
Anna made a translation of the old letter into English.

lines.text: Hello, friends! I am Lingo, your owl teacher. Hoo, hoo!
Yesterday, a news report said an archaeologist found a huge stone statue.
Archaeologists dig in the ground to find old things from long ago.
Those old things help us understand how people lived in the past.

question.text: If you could dig up one thing from the past, what would it be?

prompt.text: Look at this old clay pot. Which word is it?

explain.text: An artefact is an old object made by people, like this pot.
A metre is a unit for measuring length, about one big step.

prompt.text: A tall ____ of a famous poet stands in the park.

explain.text: A statue is a figure of a person, like the poet in the park.

prompt.text: Ancient builders cut huge ____ to make the temple walls.

explain.text: Stone is hard, and builders used it for walls.

prompt.text: A news report on TV tells people about recent events.

explain.text: A news report is a report about things that happened recently.

prompt.text: A metre measures how heavy something is.

explain.text: A metre measures length, not how heavy something is.

prompt.text: Which word is the odd one out?

explain.text: An artefact, a headdress and a statue are objects you can see and touch, but a news report is on TV or radio.

prompt.text: Which word means changing words from one language into another?

explain.text: A translation changes words from one language into another language.

lines.text: Time for a memory game! Find the matching pairs of picture and word.
Say each word out loud when you turn a card. Good luck, explorers!

prompt.text: Talk with your partner about a discovery from the past.

frames: I would like to see a ___ in a museum.
My favourite ___ is ___ because it is old and beautiful.
An archaeologist could find a ___ near my house.

model.text: I would like to see a golden headdress in a museum. My favourite artifact is a clay pot because it is very old. An archaeologist could find a statue near my house.

lines.text: Brilliant work, explorers! You learned seven new words today.
Now you can talk about the past, just like an archaeologist.

exitTicket.text: Name one artifact or statue you learned about today, and say what it is.
How many metres is one big step, and what does a translation do?
